title: Member Services Desk Manual, E.12 — A Member Paying a Refined Fuels and Propane Account Clear
content:
A member who asks to clear what stands on their account under Refined Fuels and Propane Accounts pays the money onto that account, and it is applied to the earliest-dated energy invoice standing unpaid on it. The money is taken off what the member owes, the line carries the member's own remittance reference and how the money reached the cooperative, and it is dated the day the member makes it. The member sees the payment on the next statement for the account and the balance owed drops by exactly the money paid.

The amount that clears the account is fixed only after the account carries, on every pre-buy booking whose protected floor stood above the posted price, a downside protection credit dated in the month the amount is worked out.

## Taking the payment

The payment is made with `post_energy_account_clearing_payment_6fe49ac6`. It is the member's own money and the member's own act, so the desk unlocks the tool and hands it over for the customer themselves to run; the desk does not run it for them.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `energy_account_id` | The internal reference number of the member's refined fuels or propane account the money is paid onto, as the desk reads it back from the energy account lookup |
| `invoice_number` | The energy invoice the payment is applied to, which is the one standing unpaid on the account with the earliest date on it, written as EI- followed by six digits, for example EI-440820, as it appears on the statement line being paid. No other form is accepted and it is never left empty |
| `payment_reference` | The member's own remittance reference for this payment, written as EP- followed by six digits, for example EP-118093, copied exactly as the bank or cheque carries it. No other form is accepted and it is never left empty |
| `payment_method` | How the money reaches the cooperative, one of five values: `check` where a paper cheque drawn on the member's own account is posted or handed in; `ach` where the money is sent as a bank transfer from the member's own bank; `budget_draft` where the money is taken by the standing monthly draft authorised under a level payment plan; `grain_settlement_transfer` where the money comes across from the net proceeds of a grain settlement the cooperative owes the member; `credit_card` where a card is given and the money is taken on it |
| `payment_amount_usd` | The money being paid, in USD to 2 decimal places, passed as a positive decimal number, rounded half to even to 2 decimal places on the way in, and taken off what is owed on the account |

### What comes back

A confirmation sentence naming the reference of the payment line written, the member's remittance reference, the invoice it was applied to and the money paid in USD to 2 decimal places. Receiving that sentence is what indicates the payment now stands on the account.

## The plan year behind the balance

An account that has carried a level payment plan closes its plan years against what the member actually used, and what that settling leaves stands among the instalments on the account. Before the amount that clears the account is worked out, the account must carry the true-up entry owed for every budget plan year that has passed its reconciliation date.
